why: phase-359 W10 stage C — part of the hosted PROCESS edge in `nros::env` (`packages/api/nros/src/env.rs`), the one place nano-ros calls the C library for a process facility, so `nros-c` / `nros-cpp` write their census, metadata and profile files and read `--params-file` without libstd (their image roots are `#![no_std]`). Linux targets only. rclrs has no counterpart: it is a `std` crate and uses `std::env` / `std::fs` / `std::process` directly; this is that surface for a `no_std` image inside a process. `unsafe set_var(name, value)`: `std::env::set_var` through `setenv`, `unsafe` for the same reason (the environment is not thread-safe); called only in the boot funnel, before any executor or tier task exists, to select the census recorder (`alloc`).
